Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of dry heaving and stifled sneeze (Valsalva maneuver) combined with chest X-ray findings of linear lucencies along the hilar/paratracheal regions and subcutaneous emphysema is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect). Esophageal perforation typically presents with more severe systemic toxicity and pleural effusions, which are absent here.
